topic: EEG-neurofeedback for optimising performance. II: creativity, the performing arts and ecological validity

sources.title: EEG-neurofeedback for optimising performance. II: creativity, the performing arts and ecological validity

findings.finding: Alpha/theta training provides reliable benefits for the creative performance of advanced musicians.
findings.quote: There is evidence of reliable benefits from A/T training with advanced musicians especially for creative performance

findings.finding: Both alpha/theta and sensory-motor rhythm training improve creativity, communication, and technique in novice music students.
findings.quote: reliable benefits from both A/T and SMR training for novice music performance in adults and in a school study with children with impact on creativity, communication/presentation and technique.

findings.finding: Dancers can experience performance benefits from alpha/theta and heart rate variability training protocols.
findings.quote: A/T and HRV training have benefitted dancers.

principle: Neurofeedback training, particularly using alpha/theta and sensory-motor rhythm protocols, can enhance creative performance and technical skills in the performing arts.
for_the_teacher: Incorporate heart rate variability awareness or training to help dancers manage their physiological state for better performance.
Use immersive training contexts to increase the ecological relevance of practice sessions for students.
Focus on alpha/theta training protocols to support the development of creative expression in dance students.
